properties.entry: the same grid with its rows rendered on the server

The same table as the JsonBasedDynamicDataTable example, a BeanBasedDynamicDataTable this time: its rows are rendered on the server by Wicket components, the way a DataTable renders them, and look and behave like the rows rendered in the browser from JSON.
  • The columns are Wicket's IColumns, here LambdaColumns. BeanSelectionColumn, BeanRowNumberColumn and BeanActionsColumn select, number and act on the rows; IFixedWidthColumn marks the columns that cannot be resized, IMovableColumn and IHideableColumn those the user can move and hide
  • Paging, sorting, filtering, saving, adding and deleting render the rows again via Ajax, not the whole table, so the filter in front of the navigation keeps its focus
  • The actions of a row are the same IconBasedRowActions as in the JSON example: plain markup whose clicks the table dispatches by the row's key, so a click on a user deleted in another tab still reaches the table
  • The settings above are the same as in the JSON example, each explained by its (i). Every change is posted via Ajax
  • The navigation tells how many users are selected, a SelectionCountToolbarAction, and the rows per page are chosen with the same Dropdown as the settings. "Reset the columns" is an AjaxActionButton; there is no web socket connection and no pushing of rows here
